target_customer: Indonesian creative businesses such as event organizers, agencies and concert promoters
problem: Creative-industry project businesses need working capital and financial management tools that banks and generic lenders serve poorly.
business_model: Project financing and loans plus financial management and project management software
product_category: Fintech lending and financial management for creative businesses

founders.name: Reinhart Hermanus
founders.background_notes: YC page: ex software engineer who moved into business and product management; has worked in fintech for much of his career.

competitors.name: Rey Assurance
competitors.what: Indonesian health and life insurtech (individual membership model, not employer benefits)
competitors.funding_then: Pre-seed extended in November 2021; later $4.2M seed in July 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: Lending and project management tooling for a niche was standard fintech engineering; the hard parts were underwriting and licensing partners rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Niche domain knowledge and relationships with event organizers help, but the product depends on lending partners and had no stated moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence that incumbents targeted the niche; no later news found.

market_need_then: At the time the company was Aigis, an employee health benefits and wellness platform. An AFPI director said in 2021 that only a fraction of creative-sector financing demand was met, which is the gap Finnix later targeted.

branding.domain_note: Uses finnix.id. The name collides with the long-running Finnix Linux rescue distribution at finnix.org, which dominates search results.

rebrands.why: Company pivoted from employee health benefits insurtech to creative industry finance and project management (DailySocial headline).

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press found and the name is swamped by an unrelated Linux project in search.

pivots.from: Aigis, an employee health benefits and wellness platform
pivots.to: Finnix, financing and project management for creative businesses
pivots.why: Not stated in the sources I could open; DailySocial headline reports the pivot.

outcome_analysis: The company entered YC as Aigis, an employee benefits insurtech, raised about $1M in May 2022, then pivoted to Finnix for creative-industry financing. YC lists it as active, but no later funding, traction or news was found, so the pivot's result is unknown and the cause of any stall is not public.
notes: finnix.id and the DailySocial pivot article returned 503 errors, so the pivot is known from search summaries and the headline only. The May 2022 round is attributed to Aigis (reported by DailySocial at about 14.5 billion rupiah, dated May 12, 2022 by CB Insights); the stage is not stated so it is recorded as other. CB Insights also lists a convertible note on March 29, 2022 and a total of $1.5M, and separately an aggregator lists Finnix at $500K; these conflict and are unverified. The YC page lists only one founder. Competition is for Aigis at the batch; no creative-finance competitor dated near the batch was found. Confidence is low.
